# a5view

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/belian-earth/a5view/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/belian-earth/a5view/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

a5view visualises [A5](https://a5geo.org) cells in R. [a5R](https://github.com/belian-earth/a5R) creates, indexes and transforms cells; a5view draws them, as static plots through ggplot2 or as interactive maps in the browser. Both take a vector of `a5_cell`s or a data frame with a cell column and draw the cells directly, with no conversion to polygons first.

| Task | Functions |
|------|-----------|
| Static plots | `geom_a5()`: a ggplot2 layer that works with scales, `geom_sf()` layers and any `coord_sf()` projection |
| Interactive maps | `a5_view()`: an htmlwidget built on [deck.gl](https://deck.gl) and [MapLibre](https://maplibre.org), for the viewer, R Markdown, Quarto and Shiny |
| Colour composites | `cells_rgb()`, `cells_pca_rgb()`: map several bands or an embedding to RGB, in either of the above |
| Large datasets | `a5_build_pyramid()`, `a5_view_pyramid()`: level-of-detail pyramids streamed to the browser |

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("belian-earth/a5view")
```

a5view 0.3.0 draws [A5 1.0](https://github.com/felixpalmer/a5/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) cell ids, as produced by a5R >= 0.9.9.9000. Ids written by earlier versions of a5R are valid 1.0 cells in the wrong place, so a5view cannot tell them apart and draws them where 1.0 puts them; convert them once with `a5R::a5_migrate()`. Use a5view 0.2.x for pre-1.0 ids.

## Example data

The examples below use `s2_santiago`, which ships with the package: 15,626 resolution-18 cells (about 22 m across) of a [cloud-free Sentinel-2 mosaic](https://source.coop/earthgenome/sentinel2-temporal-mosaics) over Parque O'Higgins in Santiago, Chile, with the blue, green, red and near-infrared bands.

```{r data}
library(a5view)

head(s2_santiago)
```

Sentinel-2 mosaic by Earth Genome (CC-BY 4.0). Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2023.

## Static plots with ggplot2

`geom_a5()` takes the cells through the `cell` aesthetic. `cells_rgb()` maps the red, green and blue bands to a true-colour composite; its output is already colour, so no scale is needed.

```{r ggplot-rgb, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6.5, dpi = 150}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(s2_santiago, aes(cell = cell, fill = cells_rgb(B04, B03, B02, range = c(300, 2800)))) +
  geom_a5() +
  labs(title = "Sentinel-2 true colour, Santiago 2023")
```

Any fill scale works. Like `geom_sf()`, `geom_a5()` plots in longitude and latitude by default, and `coord_sf()` reprojects the cells, here NDVI (a vegetation index) in UTM zone 19S:

```{r ggplot-utm, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6, dpi = 150}
ggplot(s2_santiago, aes(cell = cell, fill = (B08 - B04) / (B08 + B04))) +
  geom_a5() +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1, name = "NDVI") +
  coord_sf(crs = 32719) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Cells are drawn as polygons while they are large on the page and as a raster at the output resolution once they are smaller than a few pixels, so a plot of millions of cells costs about the same as one of thousands. `render = "vector"` or `"raster"` fixes the choice.

## Interactive maps

`a5_view()` draws the same data on a web map. deck.gl and [a5-js](https://github.com/felixpalmer/a5) render the cells on the GPU from their ids, so the boundaries are never computed in R. `fill` accepts a column, an expression of columns or a colour helper, as `aes()` does.

```{r interactive, screenshot.opts = list(delay = 8)}
s2_santiago$NDVI <- with(s2_santiago, (B08 - B04) / (B08 + B04))

a5_view(s2_santiago, fill = NDVI, opacity = 0.8, tooltip = c("B04", "B08"))
```

The map has:

- colour mapping through any `hcl.colors()` palette, with an on-map legend;
- basemaps from [OpenFreeMap](https://openfreemap.org) (dark, light and OSM, with no API key) and Esri satellite imagery, with labels drawn above the cells;
- a hover tooltip showing the cell id, fill value and any extra columns, and click to pin a cell;
- an opacity slider, zoom and compass control, and scale bar;
- cell borders, 3D extrusion (`elevation`) and a globe projection (`globe = TRUE`).

## Large datasets

By default a widget sends every cell to the browser, which suits small and medium datasets. For larger ones, `aggregate` builds a level-of-detail pyramid: coarser cells summarise their children (`"mean"` for scalar fields, `"rep_child"` to keep one representative child for colour composites), and the browser decodes only the levels and areas in view. `a5_build_pyramid()` writes the pyramid to a parquet file once, so it can be viewed again without rebuilding.

```r
a5_view(cells, fill = value, aggregate = "mean")

a5_build_pyramid(cells, "cells.parquet", fill = value, aggregate = "mean")
a5_view_pyramid("cells.parquet")
```

Inside Shiny the parquet file is served with HTTP range requests, so only the row groups in view are transferred.

## Shiny

`a5_viewOutput()` and `renderA5_view()` place a map in an app, and `a5_view_update()` changes its cells and colours in place without resetting the view. The hovered and clicked cells arrive as `input$<id>_hover` and `input$<id>_click`.

Setting `draw_polygon = TRUE` adds a polygon tool to the toolbar. Clicks place vertices, a double-click closes the polygon, and the polygon arrives as WKT at `input$<id>_polygon_draw`. The widget does not highlight the cells inside it: resolve the WKT to cells on the server and send new fills with `a5_view_update()`.

```r
a5_viewOutput("map")

# server
output$map <- renderA5_view({
  a5_view(my_cells, draw_polygon = TRUE)
})

observeEvent(input$map_polygon_draw, {
  cells_in_poly <- a5R::a5_polygon_to_cells(
    wk::wkt(input$map_polygon_draw),
    resolution = 4L
  ) |>
    a5R::a5_uncompact()
  # ... use cells_in_poly, e.g. a5_view_update() with selection-driven fills.
})
```

See `inst/examples/polygon-select/app.R` for a complete app combining click and polygon selection.
